beats.role_note: walker mode B00 — ClaudeComposerAsk. Prompt begins 'Please use Walker to convert my game design document about …'. Labelled on screen as an illustrative reconstruction (not a transcript). Liam introduces himself in the first breath.
beats.narration_text: Hola — this is Liam, in for Bear. Jiean Yin took Nik Bear Brown's walker-jumpman starter and extended it, following Walker's workflow, with Claude Code: a new hero and a new climb. This composer prompt is an illustrative reconstruction, not a transcript. Everything after it is the real game.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about extending walker-jumpman — a helmeted spear-carrier and a four-landing climb with spike traps — into a playable Godot project. Keep the single jump, the controls and the quick retry.
output: Level extended; finish moved to the top.

beats.role_note: walker mode B01 — what was built, hesitant-writer overview. Correction: 'rebuilt' -> 'extended' (it is an extension of the starter, not a new game). States the slice's limits.
beats.narration_text: What was built. Level one of walker-jumpman — two gaps, a spike and a flag — kept as it was: same jump, same controls, same quick retry. On top of it, a helmeted spear-carrier replaces the blue block, and a new section called Climb adds four landings stepping upward, two of them guarded by spikes, with the flag moved to the top. No cherries, no sound, no new abilities.

props.text:
Walker Jumpman, rebuilt.
Same jump. Same quick retry.
A new hero. A new climb.

beats.role_note: Cause->effect from source. ClaudeCodeBeat with a verbatim excerpt of godot/game/session.gd at film-source-v1 (lines 98-104 plus the two call sites at lines 78 and 221). Editor chrome is reconstructed; code is actual. Display: tabs rendered as two spaces and the long teeth.append line wrapped at its commas (marked on screen); tokens are verbatim. brandLabel omitted: one handle per film, on the outro (OUTRO-LOCK); it also tripped the card-clip check.
beats.narration_text: Here's the cause behind spikes that appear exactly where they kill. The starter drew spikes at a hard-coded floor height. Moving only the level data put the new spikes' collision on top of the landings, but drew them inside the pillars. Now one function builds the triangles, and both the collision shapes and the drawing use it.

shot.label: Actual source excerpt · reconstructed editor view

props.title: godot/game/session.gd — film-source-v1
props.code:
# line 98 (tabs shown as two spaces)
static func spike_triangles(rect: Rect2) -> Array[PackedVector2Array]:
  var teeth: Array[PackedVector2Array] = []
  var w := rect.size.x / 3.0
  for i in range(3):
    var x := rect.position.x + float(i) * w
    # one line in the source, wrapped here at its commas:
    teeth.append(PackedVector2Array([Vector2(x, rect.end.y),
        Vector2(x + w / 2.0, rect.position.y), Vector2(x + w, rect.end.y)]))
  return teeth

# line 78 — collision
    for points in spike_triangles(rect):
# line 221 — drawing
    for points in spike_triangles(
        Rect2(entry[0], entry[1], entry[2], entry[3])):  # wrapped here
props.sparkLine: One set of triangles feeds both the collision and the drawing.

The game shown is the revision tagged film-source-v1.

beats.role_note: Verdict: observed working vs defects vs untested vs planned; one concrete next improvement.
beats.narration_text: Verdict. Observed working: the new character, all four landings, both spike traps, the relocated finish, retry and replay. Defects: the results card says one retries, and a jump looks the same as standing still. Untested: whether a newcomer reads the second landing's spikes before dying — the only human tester is the author. Pause on focus loss is checked by a test, not shown here. Next improvement: a clearer cue before landing two, and distinct poses in the air.

artifactLines: Works on screen: new hero, four landings, both traps, finish, retry, replay.
Defects: '1 retries' on the results card; jumping uses the idle pose.
Untested: newcomers — one human tester, the author. Focus-loss pause: test only.
Next: a clearer cue before landing two; distinct airborne poses.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Use Walker on your own copy of walker-jumpman: add one new landing after the finish plateau without touching tuning dot g d.
